metaDescription: Lost Creek, Harrison County mineral owners: legacy shallow wells, Marcellus corridor proximity, and family-farm heirship title work.
heroLead: Lost Creek is a small Harrison County community where legacy shallow gas production and newer Marcellus activity both touch the surrounding farmland.
intro: Harrison County has a long production history that predates modern horizontal drilling by decades, and Lost Creek's rural acreage carries some of that legacy — older wellbores drilled under leases signed well before the Marcellus era, alongside newer development pushing in from more active parts of the county.

sections.heading: Legacy production and older lease terms
paragraphs: Wells around Lost Creek that predate the Marcellus boom were often leased under terms that look very different from a modern agreement — lower royalty percentages, sometimes flat-rate payment structures. If your family's interest is under one of these older leases, it's worth checking whether the terms reflect current West Virginia law or whether a conversion is available.

sections.heading: Family-farm heirship near Lost Creek
paragraphs: As with much of rural Harrison County, mineral interests around Lost Creek have typically stayed within the same families for generations, splitting further with each inheritance. A tract that started as one owner's interest a century ago can now be divided among a dozen or more descendants, some local and some scattered well outside the county.

sections.heading: How a courthouse title check narrows down what you actually hold
paragraphs: For a family tract near Lost Creek that's changed hands informally across generations, a title check starts with the earliest recorded severance and works forward through every subsequent conveyance, lease, and probate filing. The result is a clear percentage figure rather than a rough family estimate of what 'your share' amounts to.

This matters most when a well is newly permitted nearby: a confirmed percentage lets you evaluate an offer — whether from an operator wanting to lease or a buyer wanting to purchase the interest outright — against an actual number instead of a guess.

faqs.question: Is my Lost Creek lease paying a flat rate or a royalty?
faqs.answer: Check the payment clause on your original lease or division order. Flat-rate arrangements were common on older Harrison County leases and can often be converted to a royalty basis under state law.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically share an old Lost Creek family tract?
faqs.answer: It varies, but interests split across five to ten or more living heirs after multiple generations are common in this area.

faqs.question: Where are the records for my Lost Creek mineral interest filed?
faqs.answer: At the Harrison County Courthouse in Clarksburg, which holds the deed, will, and lease books needed to trace your chain of title.

faqs.question: Do I need to wait for a new well to be permitted before checking my title?
faqs.answer: No, it's worth confirming your ownership percentage regardless of current drilling activity so you're prepared either way.
